title: “The kings of Sheba and Seba” and “the gold of Sheba” — the Greek has “kings of the Arabians and Saba” and “the gold of Arabia”
summary: The KJV names Sheba and Seba at 72:10 and Sheba at 72:15. Brenton’s Greek has “Arabians” and Saba at 72:10 and “Arabia” at 72:15.
text: KJV Psalms 72:10: “The kings of Tarshish and of the isles shall bring presents: the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.” KJV 72:15: “to him shall be given of the gold of Sheba” Hebrew (WLC) 72:10: מַלְכֵ֥י שְׁבָ֥א וּ֝סְבָ֗א אֶשְׁכָּ֥ר יַקְרִֽיבוּ. Brenton’s Greek 71:15: ἐκ τοῦ χρυσίου τῆς Ἀραβίας [of the gold of Arabia]. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/72/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA071.htm.
reasoning: In the Hebrew and the KJV the two names at 72:10 are Sheba and Seba, and the name at 72:15 is the first of them. In the Greek the first name at 72:10 is a people (“of Arabians”), the second is Saba, and the name at 72:15 is “Arabia”.
scope: This compares the wording of three texts. It does not show which wording is original.
